proves: a border with square corners paints as a border, and so do the rounded and per-edge cases beside it
checkable: 200x72, three 56x56 cells at y=8..63 on white, blue #2850dc border over red #dc2828. Cell 0 is x=8..63, cell 1 x=72..127, cell 2 x=136..191. FOUR SAMPLES, one per edge, because a box has four edges and one row can read only two of them. Top, row 8: cell 0 blue 8-63, its whole 6 border across the width. Left and right, row 35: cell 0 blue 8-13, red 14-57, blue 58-63; cell 1 blue 72-77, red 78-121, blue 122-127; cell 2 blue 136-149 (the 14 left), red 150-181, blue 182-191 (the 10 right). Bottom, row 60: cell 0 blue 8-63, cell 1 blue 76-123, cell 2 blue 136-191 - three bars of the full cell width, no red anywhere in them. Row 63, the last row of the cells, is the same three bars.
regression: cell 0 rendered a diagonal wedge across half the box. box_path built a square box with Skia's add_rect and a rounded one by extending a path, while ring_path's inner contour always took the second; mixed, the two contours joined into one self-intersecting path and the even-odd fill left the wedge. A square box is now a rounded one with every radius at zero.
why-three: the failure was one branch of a two-branch function, so a fixture with only the square cell would pass if the rounded branch broke instead. The third cell takes the per-edge path, which is a branch neither of the other two exercises - borders-per-edge covers it only with a radius.
why-nothing-caught-it: every bordered golden in the suite before this one sets a corner radius, so none of them took the broken branch.
why-this-fixture-did-not-catch-the-rest: for its first day it sampled row 35 alone. That row crosses the left and right edges and neither the top nor the bottom, so a picture whose bottom edge was a diagonal wedge read as correct in a fixture written for exactly that wedge - the defect survived at an eighth of its original area and the showcase found it by drawing a picture a person looked at. Three cells, a control and a third branch could not help: the cells were what varied and the sample point was not. A probe that reads one row of a box with four edges measures one edge and reports on four.
status: measured from the committed image; correct behaviour, not a pinned defect. The bottom-edge wedge that this file recorded earlier today is fixed, and rows 8, 60 and 63 above are what now guards it.
mitre-antialiasing-moved-once: 57 pixels of this image changed when the corner division was fixed, all of them on the mitre diagonals of the per-edge cell, and all of them blends of the same two edge colours before and after. No geometry moved there: a seam between two clipped fills rasterises slightly differently through a half-plane than through a polygon vertex, which is a different arithmetic path to the same shape. The corners that did move are in borders-per-edge, and they are pinned against Chrome in crates/meo-canvas-core/tests/chrome_corner_truth.rs.
